# Copilot instructions

Owner: greenblacked (Serhii). Applies to Copilot Chat, Copilot code review and the Copilot coding agent.

Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) first: they are the rules for this repo. If they disagree, CONTRIBUTING.md and the scripts in `scripts/ci/` win.

Path-scoped rules for `src/`, `e2e/`, CI files and pull request reviews are in `.github/instructions/` (`*.instructions.md`).

## Repo gates
- Use pnpm, never npm. Set up pnpm with `./scripts/ci/pnpm-pin.sh install` then `verify` (AGENTS.md, Setup), then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- Before every push run `pnpm run check` (lint, typecheck, unit tests, `scripts/ci/hygiene.sh`, `scripts/ci/links.sh`). Also run `./scripts/ci/tokens.sh` and `./scripts/ci/commits.sh origin/stage..HEAD`.
- UI changes also need `pnpm run build && pnpm run test:e2e` (use `--project=<name>`). Say which could not run.
- Tests never reach a live vendor. Only `pnpm run source-health` probes vendors, and it is not part of tests or reviews.
- A user-visible change adds a line under `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`, and a behaviour change updates the README in the same commit. Docs-only, CI-only and refactor-only changes need no entry.
- Flow is `dev` -> `stage` -> `main`, merge commits only. Work is committed straight to `dev`, only after all local checks pass. Automated reviews (Codex, Copilot code review) run only on pull requests whose base is `stage` or `main`; for any other base, reply that and stop.

## Serhii's standing rules
- No tooling attribution anywhere published (commits, PR titles and bodies, issues, comments, code, docs): no "Generated by/with" footers, no Co-authored-by trailer for Copilot or any AI tool, no session links, no model names. After a PR is created, re-read its body and remove any appended footer. The Copilot coding agent may add its own branch prefix or trailers; avoid them where you can, otherwise flag it in the PR instead of claiming compliance.
- Branches: `<feature|fix|docs|ci|chore|refactor|test|perf|build>/<short-kebab>`, 2 to 5 words, 50 characters max (`scripts/ci/branch.sh`). `fb/` is retired. Never use a tool-named prefix.
- Commits: author `greenblacked <23718180+greenblacked@users.noreply.github.com>`; Conventional Commits, imperative, subject <= 72 characters, no trailing period; one logical change per commit so each can be reverted alone; one PR per request. Releases use type `release` (`release: X.Y.Z`, PR `release: vX.Y.Z`), never `chore(release)`.
- Never push unreviewed or unverified work, not even to get a PR up sooner. Review your own diff adversarially (bugs, edge cases, security, missing tests, docs) and fix what you find before pushing.
- Never merge and never promote (`dev` -> `stage`, `stage` -> `main`): the owner does both. Never force-push or rewrite pushed history. Tell Serhii about branches to delete.
- Copilot coding agent: its PR must target `dev` (never `stage` or `main`) and is only a proposal; the owner lands it on `dev`. Its `copilot/` branch will not pass `branch.sh`; do not expect it to.
- Owner's merge condition: every check on the PR head green, and the target's latest push CI green.
- Owner's Codex gate: both the Codex Security Review and Code Review must be finished on the PR's current head (a new push restarts the wait). Read every comment and thread, fix or answer each, and resolve every thread before merging. Do not post `@codex review` on the `dev` -> `stage` PR.
- Owner, before promoting: `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/stage origin/dev`.
- A UI bug reported on one phone is a mobile bug: fix and test across mobile browsers and versions (Android Chrome and others, iOS Safari old and new, phones and tablets, all three backgrounds), use feature detection with a fallback, and add regression tests that fail before the fix.
- Never put secrets, tokens, keys or `.env` contents in code, commits, PRs or docs. If you find one, report only its path.
